critical_issues.msg: `server_default="0"` passes a Python string to PostgreSQL for an INTEGER column — if the DB default is cast incorrectly, the column may store text "0" instead of integer 0.
critical_issues.suggestion: Use `server_default=sa.text("0")` or pass raw integers `server_default=0` without quotes, for all integer columns (revoked, sign_count, enabled).

critical_issues.msg: Same string-default issue as line 34 for `sign_count` INTEGER column.
Same string-default issue for `enabled` INTEGER column.
Index `ix_refresh_tokens_user_id` is created twice — once inside `create_table()` kwargs and once explicitly at line 39. PostgreSQL will error on the duplicate.
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove the `index=True` from the `sa.Column` definition for user_id inside `create_table` since the explicit `op.create_index` at line 39 already creates it. Or remove line 39 and keep the inline `index=True`.

critical_issues.msg: `UserModel` is referenced but never imported — NameError at runtime when `/webauthn/verify` is called.
critical_issues.suggestion: Add import: `from db.models.users import UserModel` at the top of the file.

critical_issues.msg: Route `/devices` (delete) is defined before `/devices/{device_fingerprint}` — FastAPI matches static segments first, so DELETE /devices will always hit the handler at line 505, making the per-device delete at line 491 unreachable.
critical_issues.suggestion: Swap the order: define `delete /devices/{device_fingerprint}` before `delete /devices`, or use a path parameter on a single endpoint with optional query params.

critical_issues.msg: The router declares `response_model=LoginResponse` but the function returns a raw `fastapi.Response` object — the response_model is ignored entirely, and HTTP status code is implicitly 200 instead of any declared code.
critical_issues.suggestion: Use `response_class=Response` and explicitly set `status_code=200` on the Response, or return the Pydantic model and use FastAPI's `.set_cookie()` method on the response object instead of manual headers.

critical_issues.msg: RBAC models (RoleModel, PermissionModel, RolePermissionModel, UserRoleModel) are imported and listed in __all__ in rbac.py but are absent from this re-export, breaking external imports.
critical_issues.suggestion: Add to imports: from db.models.rbac import PermissionModel, RoleModel, RolePermissionModel, UserRoleModel and add all four to the __all__ list.

critical_issues.msg: public_key column is String(1024) but WebAuthn ES256 public keys are 32 bytes (44 Base64 chars) and RS256 keys are 256+ bytes; FIDO2 attestation objects (X.509 cert chains) routinely exceed 1024 chars Base64-encoded.
critical_issues.suggestion: Change String(1024) to String(2048) or larger (or use Text) to accommodate all WebAuthn key sizes and attestation formats.

critical_issues.msg: Challenge is returned to the caller in plaintext with no server-side storage or expiry. An attacker who intercepts the registration response can replay the same challenge on a different device, defeating WebAuthn's phishing protection.
critical_issues.suggestion: Store the challenge server-side (e.g. Redis) with a TTL of ~60s and a unique registration ID; return only the registration ID to the client. Verify the challenge against the stored record in finish_registration.

critical_issues.msg: Registration verification is a stub: `origin`, `challenge`, and `rpId` are parsed but never validated. A malicious client can submit arbitrary attestation data.
critical_issues.suggestion: Validate origin matches expected rpId origin, challenge matches the stored server-side value, and attestation structure before storing the credential.

critical_issues.msg: Assertion verification is a stub: `origin` and `challenge` are read but never verified against expected values, allowing replay or cross-site assertion injection.
critical_issues.suggestion: Retrieve the expected challenge from server-side storage using the user_id/session as key and validate it; reject if missing or expired.

suggestions.msg: `public_key` column uses VARCHAR(1024) but WebAuthn public keys are binary data (CBOR-encoded) that can exceed 1024 bytes for some ECDAA keys.
suggestions.suggestion: Use `sa.Column("public_key", sa.Text(), nullable=False)` or `sa.LargeBinary()` instead of `sa.String(length=1024)`.

suggestions.msg: No composite index on (user_id, revoked) exists for refresh_tokens — queries filtering by user_id AND revoked status will scan the full user_id index.
suggestions.suggestion: Add `op.create_index("ix_refresh_tokens_user_id_revoked", "refresh_tokens", ["user_id", "revoked"])` after line 39 for faster token revocation lookups.

suggestions.msg: No composite index on (user_id, trusted) exists for device_trust — listing trusted devices per user would benefit from a composite index.
suggestions.suggestion: Add `op.create_index("ix_device_trust_user_id_trusted", "device_trust", ["user_id", "trusted"])` after line 80.

issues.message: public_key column is String(1024) but WebAuthn ES256 public keys are 32 bytes (44 Base64 chars) and RS256 keys are 256+ bytes; FIDO2 attestation objects (X.509 cert chains) routinely exceed 1024 chars Base64-encoded.
issues.suggestion: Change String(1024) to String(2048) or larger (or use Text) to accommodate all WebAuthn key sizes and attestation formats.

issues.message: Column 'enabled' is typed as Integer with Python default 1 but the attribute is annotated bool and to_dict() casts it to bool — Integer is stored but bool is expected.
issues.suggestion: Use Boolean (from sqlalchemy import Boolean) instead of Integer: enabled: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, default=True, nullable=False)

parsed.summary: public_key column has an undersized VARCHAR limit that will truncate valid WebAuthn credentials; enabled column also uses Integer instead of Boolean.

issues.message: New DeviceTrustModel created in trust_device sets trusted=True but never sets trusted_at, making first-trust timestamps unreliable.
issues.suggestion: Add trusted_at=datetime.now(UTC) to the DeviceTrustModel constructor at line 82.

issues.message: Existing device update path in trust_device sets last_used_at but not trusted_at, so trusted_at only records the first trust event.
issues.suggestion: Add model.trusted_at = datetime.now(UTC) inside the else block at line 93.

issues.message: check_suspicious_activity detects IP change but the SuspiciousActivityReason.GEO_CHANGE path is never triggered; the geo check is commented out with no fallback, so geo changes go undetected.
issues.suggestion: Either wire up a geo-IP check or remove the GEO_CHANGE reason entirely to avoid misleading consumers of this method.

issues.message: generate_device_fingerprint silently accepts an empty fingerprint for all-None inputs, producing a deterministic hash for all unidentified devices.
issues.suggestion: Consider returning an empty string or None when all inputs are None to avoid conflating unknown devices.

issues.message: ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRY_MINUTES and REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRY_DAYS are hardcoded module-level constants rather than loaded from settings, breaking the 'Config separated from code' rule (guideline 7).
issues.suggestion: Move these to configs/settings.py and reference them here, e.g. settings.access_token_expiry_minutes.

issues.message: expires_at datetime comparison uses .replace(tzinfo=UTC) which assumes the DB-stored datetime is naive; if the model stores timezone-aware datetimes this will raise a TypeError.
issues.suggestion: Verify the RefreshTokenModel.expires_at column type; if it's already timezone-aware, remove the .replace() call and compare directly.

issues.message: rotate_refresh_token uses .replace(tzinfo=UTC) on expires_at for expiry check, same tz-awareness assumption risk as line 132.
issues.suggestion: Unify expiry checking logic to avoid duplicating the same potential bug across two methods.

parsed.summary: Token lifecycle is well-implemented with proper hashing and revocation; config constants are hardcoded and there is a timezone-awareness mismatch risk in expiry checks.

issues.message: Bare `except Exception` swallows all errors including `json.JSONDecodeError`, making debugging and security logging difficult.
issues.suggestion: Catch `json.JSONDecodeError` specifically and re-raise a meaningful ValueError.

issues.message: Bare `except Exception` silently falls through to empty auth_data_bytes; the failure is invisible and unaudited.
issues.suggestion: Catch specific decode exceptions and log a warning so security events are observable.

issues.message: Service raises raw `ValueError` instead of the project exception pattern (`ValidationException`), so the global handler won't produce structured JSON error responses.
issues.suggestion: Replace `raise ValueError(...)` with `raise ValidationException(...)` from pkg.errors.app_exceptions.

issues.message: Service raises raw `ValueError` instead of the project exception pattern (`ValidationException`).
issues.suggestion: Replace with `raise ValidationException("Possible credential clone detected — signature counter not incremented")`.

issues.message: Challenge is returned to the caller in plaintext with no server-side storage or expiry. An attacker who intercepts the registration response can replay the same challenge on a different device, defeating WebAuthn's phishing protection.
issues.suggestion: Store the challenge server-side (e.g. Redis) with a TTL of ~60s and a unique registration ID; return only the registration ID to the client. Verify the challenge against the stored record in finish_registration.

issues.message: Registration verification is a stub: `origin`, `challenge`, and `rpId` are parsed but never validated. A malicious client can submit arbitrary attestation data.
issues.suggestion: Validate origin matches expected rpId origin, challenge matches the stored server-side value, and attestation structure before storing the credential.

issues.message: Assertion verification is a stub: `origin` and `challenge` are read but never verified against expected values, allowing replay or cross-site assertion injection.
issues.suggestion: Retrieve the expected challenge from server-side storage using the user_id/session as key and validate it; reject if missing or expired.

issues.message: The anti-cloning guard `if credential.sign_count > 0` skips clone detection for brand-new credentials (sign_count==0), allowing a cloned credential to be registered as valid on first use.
issues.suggestion: Set sign_count to 1 on initial storage (not 0) so the guard catches cloned credentials from first assertion, or document the trade-off explicitly.

issues.message: Model defines `enabled: Mapped[bool]` but the column type is `Integer` (0/1 storage). The type annotation is misleading; SQLAlchemy will store bool as integer anyway.
issues.suggestion: Use `Boolean()` column type from sqlalchemy, or annotate as `Mapped[int]` to match the actual storage.

parsed.summary: WebAuthn service implements registration and assertion flows but skips all cryptographic verifications (origin, challenge, attestation) and returns challenges in plaintext, making it vulnerable to replay attacks in production.
